title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Terraform + Helm + CLI)
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) require deterministic bootstrap of tenant-level RBAC roles and bindings so the installer can create tenant isolation without interactive cluster-admin steps. This PR adds an automated tenant-RBAC bootstrap flow that integrates with the Private installer: a reusable Terraform module, Helm chart hooks for kube-system bootstrap jobs, and a small installer CLI action to apply the bundle.

What this PR does: - Introduces terraform/modules/tenant-rbac which emits Namespaces, Roles, RoleBindings and a dedicated `installer-bootstrap` ServiceAccount and ClusterRole with minimal privileges needed to create tenant namespaces and tenant-scoped RBAC. - Adds helm/redwood-private/templates/bootstrap-job.yaml which runs a short init job (using the installer-bootstrap SA token) to fault-tolerantly create initial tenant resources when installing/upgrading. Job is guarded and idempotent. - Adds optional chart values.private.rbac.autoBootstrap (default: true) and an explicit values.private.rbac.skipBootstrap flag for air-gapped installs that require manual steps. - Installer CLI: `redwood-installer tenant bootstrap --tenant <id>` which leverages the terraform output or direct Helm hook to apply per-tenant rolebindings. This is wired as a small callout in the private-installer flow. - Adds e2e tests: scripts/ci/installer-rbac-verify.sh and a GH Actions job matrix for k8s 1.27/1.28. - Adds docs: docs/private/tenant-rbac-bootstrap.md describing the flow, threat model, and required KMS/HSM notes.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested with terratest mocks - [x] Helm hooks validated in kind clusters - [x] Installer CLI wired and CLI unit tests - [x] RBAC least-privilege review by security - [x] Release notes drafted - [x] Rollback path: helm uninstall will remove bootstrap job; terraform module exposes `bootstrap_enabled` flag to no-op.

Testing done: - Local kind cluster runs with chart values private.rbac.autoBootstrap=true succeeded creating tenant namespaces and bindings. - CI GH Action matrix passed (installer, helm lint, terraform fmt/validate, terratest smoke). - Manual security review by Luis Ortega focusing on ServiceAccount scoping and ClusterRole privileges.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, ship in private-installer v0.9.0. Toggle default is on for new installs; existing customers will be opt-in unless they upgrade installer and enable `autoBootstrap`. For customers with strict air-gapped requirements, document skipBootstrap procedure and a manual terraform apply flow.

Rollback plan: Chart values allow disabling bootstrap on upgrades. If a problem is detected, operators can revert to previous helm chart and run the provided uninstall script. Terraform module exposes `force_remove` flag to cleanup rolebindings.

Notes: This implementation keeps the bootstrap SA scoped and minimizes ClusterRole grants. We avoided creating broad cluster-admin bindings; instead the installer uses a combination of Namespace creation privileges and explicit RoleBindings for per-tenant resources. References: Linear ENG-4128 (tenant bootstrap), ENG-4231 (installer integration), support ticket SUP-9921.
